# ROADMAP: Andes V5 CSR transport for bare-metal hybrid

Goal: extend the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff to carry the Andes-specific architectural
state a bare-metal Andes Core needs, so the vsim leg resumes with the same
memory system / extension setup the functional leg booted into. Source of truth
for CSR numbers + semantics: `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf` (Table 6 Andes
M-mode, Table 11 Andes U-mode, sec 9.8 PMA).

## STATUS — F0 + F1 DONE and e2e-validated (stopped at F1 by request)

The key design decision: a single X-macro (`HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST` in the ABI
header) drives all four consumers (plugin drain, ResumeDriver restore,
StateDrain re-read, driver state_diff verify), so a scalar Andes CSR is wired
once, not per-feature; PMA arrays mirror the existing PMP loops. A side effect
of that DRY design: building the machinery for F1 (uitb/jvt) also wired the
other 11 scalars (F2/F4-F8) and PMA (F3) through all four sites in the same
loops -- their transport code + unit tests are in, even though only F1 was
finalized/validated this pass.

Verified:
- ABI layout lock: `state_abi.test.cpp` (v3, 126 assertions).
- restore: `resume_driver.test.cpp` (every Andes CSR + PMA, 392 assertions).
- re-read: `state_drain.test.cpp` (whole block round-trip, 604 assertions).
- verify: `driver/state_diff_test.cpp` (per-feature field probes, all pass).
- plugin drain compiles clean; the real Andes QEMU (`target/riscv/andes_csr.c`)
  exposes every gdb mnemonic used (mxstatus/pmacfg/uitb/ucode/jvt/...).
- **e2e** (real QEMU -> vsim, `ax45mpv_premium` rebuilt with the new code):
  `./andesim run --mode hybrid --verify rt_csr_survival.elf` -> `state-diff
  PASS: 144 fields match`. The Andes block round-trips on hardware.

e2e finding (folded in): `msp_bound`/`msp_base` are engine-reset-divergent --
QEMU resets them to all-ones, the vsim `ax45mpv_premium` RTL has no HW stack
protection so it drains 0. Transported tolerantly, but **verify-excluded** like
`mip` (state_diff.cpp). Not a transport bug.

Not done (out of this F1 pass): the silicon-behavior fixtures that drive a
*non-zero* uitb (CoDense `exec.it`), real DSP `ucode`, real PMA regions, etc.;
and rebuilding the non-premium vsim configs (mp2/advanced/d23/makatau still
carry v2 -- a handoff on those now version-mismatches until rebuilt).

Scope (confirmed): full envelope -- CoDense+Zcmt, DSP/P-ext, Local Memory +
throttle + stack protection, PMA. ABI strategy (confirmed): bump to v3 with a
dedicated Andes block.

## Mental model: 4 transport classes

- **Class 0 config/RO** (`0xFCx/0xFDx`, crash-save): NOT transported. Hardwired
  per core; QEMU `-cpu` must equal vsim RTL. Optional one-time consistency assert.
- **Class 1 boot-static setup**: crt0 writes once before ROI, ROI mostly reads.
  drain + restore (like today's `mcache_ctl`). Most fields below.
- **Class 2 live arch state**: changes inside the ROI -> full round-trip
  (drain + restore + re-drain + `state_diff` verify), like `vxsat`. Only `ucode`.
- **Class 3 trap/interrupt state** (`mdcause`, `msave*`, CLIC, NMI vectors): NOT
  in scope; ROI is trap-free/interrupt-free. Deferred to the S/U-envelope work.

## Per-feature precondition (every feature's first RED check)

The plugin drains via QEMU gdbstub `find_reg(name)`; restore writes via vsim DMI.
So each CSR is transportable only if (1) QEMU gdbstub exports the name AND
(2) vsim DMI can write it. The unit test asserts both handles exist; if either is
missing the engine/QEMU lacks that extension and the field stays zero (tolerant
no-op via `write_csr_tolerant`). Zero in the wire format always means "producer
did not have this CSR".

## The 3 repos every feature (except F0) touches

| Repo | Path | Role |
|------|------|------|
| `andesim_abi` (submodule) | `hybrid/state_abi.h`, `hybrid/state_abi_check.h` | wire struct + layout lock -- **F0 only** |
| `andesim` | `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` | drain (gdbstub read) |
| `andesim` | `driver/state_diff.{hpp,cpp}` (+ `state_diff_test.cpp`) | `--verify` compare |
| `andesim` | `tests/fixtures/*` | RED fixtures |
| `hybrid_vsim` (external `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim`) | `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` | restore (DMI write; extend the `write_csr_tolerant` list / PMP-style loop) |
| `hybrid_vsim` (external) | `src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` | re-drain (DMI read at exit halt) |

Dedup targets (Coding Principle: don't duplicate): restore reuses
`write_csr_tolerant(addr,val)`; PMA reuses the existing `pmpaddr`/`pmpcfg` loop
shape; drain reuses the `find_reg` + `read_reg64` pattern.

---

## F0 - v3 ABI + dedicated Andes block  [BLOCKS ALL OTHERS]

Status: TODO. Deps: none.

Define the whole Andes block ONCE so F1..F8 only populate existing fields (no
later offset reshuffle -> features stay independent). Bump
`HYBRID_STATE_VERSION` 2 -> 3; add `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES (1u<<3)` to gate the block
live; all three readers reject version<3 by magic+version+size.

Proposed block (LE u64; zero = "producer lacked it"):

```c
struct hybrid_andes_csr {     // v3
  uint64_t mxstatus;          // 0x7C4  Andes mstatus companion (DME/IME/PFT_EN)
  uint64_t mpft_ctl;          // 0x7C5  perf throttling (T_LEVEL)
  uint64_t mclk_ctl;          // 0x7DF  clock control
  uint64_t milmb;             // 0x7C0  ILM base + enable
  uint64_t mdlmb;             // 0x7C1  DLM base + enable
  uint64_t mecc_code;         // 0x7C2  ECC code
  uint64_t mhsp_ctl;          // 0x7C6  HW stack protection control
  uint64_t msp_bound;         // 0x7C7
  uint64_t msp_base;          // 0x7C8
  uint64_t mcountermask_m;    // 0x7D1  counter mask (cycle hygiene)
  uint64_t uitb;              // 0x800  CoDense instruction table base
  uint64_t jvt;               // 0x017  Zcmt jump vector table
  uint64_t ucode;             // 0x801  DSP/P-ext overflow flag (Class 2)
  uint64_t pmacfg[2];         // 0xBC0, 0xBC2 (RV64: 16 entries / 2 regs)
  uint64_t pmaaddr[16];       // 0xBD0..0xBDF
};                            // 31 u64 = 248 bytes; recompute reserved[]
```

Key files: `hybrid/state_abi.h`, `hybrid/state_abi_check.h`; size/version gate in
`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`, vsim `state_loader.hpp`/`state_drain.hpp`, and
`driver/state_diff.cpp`. Coordinated: edit `andesim_abi`, then bump the submodule
pointer in BOTH `andesim/include` and `hybrid_vsim/external/andesim_abi`.

RED: `state_abi.test.cpp` asserts `version==3`, `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES`, and
`offsetof`/`sizeof` of the new block + every named field (layout lock). All
fields zero on legacy producers.

---

## F1 - CoDense + Zcmt table bases (`uitb` 0x800, `jvt` 0x017)  [DONE]

Status: DONE + e2e-validated. Deps: F0. Class 1. uitb/jvt are X-list entries,
wired through plugin drain / resume / re-read / verify; round-trip confirmed by
the rt_csr_survival hybrid+verify run (PASS, 144 fields). A CoDense fixture that
sets a *non-zero* uitb and runs `exec.it` inside the ROI is the remaining
deeper check (proves the value is used, not just transported).

RED fixture: ROI uses `exec.it` (needs `uitb`) and/or `cm.jt`/`cm.jalt` (needs
`jvt`); without transport it faults or mis-executes in vsim. Plus round-trip:
write sentinel pre-ROI, read back inside ROI, `--verify` drain==restore.

GREEN: drain `uitb`/`jvt`; restore via `write_csr_tolerant`; re-drain; compare.

---

## F2 - `mxstatus` (0x7C4)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Andes companion to `mstatus` (DME/IME misalign
exception enable, PFT_EN). Writable M-mode -> full round-trip + verify (model on
`mscratch`). RED: fixture sets `mxstatus` sentinel pre-ROI, reads inside, verify.

---

## F3 - PMA: `pmacfg0/2` + `pmaaddr0..15` (0xBC0/2, 0xBD0..DF)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Biggest + highest correctness/cycle impact.
Memory attributes (cacheable / device / NAPOT). Reuse the `pmpaddr`/`pmpcfg`
loop shape in `resume_driver.hpp`. Gated on `mmsc_cfg.PPMA`.

RED fixture: mark an MMIO region device-type + a RAM region cacheable via PMA
pre-ROI; without transport vsim resumes PMA-reset -> wrong cache/device behavior.
Assert via cycle delta (cacheable RAM) and/or a device-ordering check.

---

## F4 - DSP `ucode` (0x801)  [Class 2]

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. The P-ext overflow (OV) flag is LIVE state, like `vxsat`:
restore BEFORE the ROI, re-drain AFTER, `state_diff` compares it. Gated on P-ext.
RED: DSP op sets OV; round-trip must preserve the bit.

---

## F5 - Local Memory `milmb` (0x7C0), `mdlmb` (0x7C1) [+ `mecc_code` 0x7C2]

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Base+enable of ILM/DLM. Only live if the linker
script places sections in LM (check `runtime/andesim.ld`). RED: place a hot array
in DLM; transport keeps vsim accessing fast LM (cycle delta) vs DRAM/fault.

---

## F6 - Throttle / clock `mpft_ctl` (0x7C5), `mclk_ctl` (0x7DF)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. Cycle-only. Pairs with `mxstatus.PFT_EN` (F2):
if throttling is enabled, the resumed leg must throttle identically or the cycle
figure diverges. RED: enable throttle pre-ROI, assert cycle delta matches.

---

## F7 - HW stack protection `mhsp_ctl` (0x7C6), `msp_bound` (0x7C7), `msp_base` (0x7C8)

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Class 1. If crt0 enables stack overflow/underflow
detection, the bounds must survive or vsim either misses protection or
false-traps. RED: enable + set bounds pre-ROI; ROI stack access stays in-bounds.

---

## F8 - Counter mask `mcountermask_m` (0x7D1) [+ `mcountinhibit` 0x320]

Status: TODO. Deps: F0. Cycle-figure hygiene: controls whether `mcycle`/
`minstret` advance in M-mode. RED: set mask pre-ROI, assert the cycle figure
reflects it.

---

## Out of scope (record, do not implement now)

- Class 0 config/RO: `micm_cfg`/`mdcm_cfg`/`mmsc_cfg*`/`mvec_cfg`/`mrvarch_cfg*`/
  `mhvm*`/`mpl2cm_cfg`/`ml1dbf_cfg`/`mccache_ctl_base`, crash-save. (consistency
  assert only, optional later feature.)
- Class 3 trap/NMI/CLIC: `mdcause`, `mslideleg`, `msavestatus`/`msaveepc{1,2}`/
  `msavecause{1,2}`/`msavedcause{1,2}`, `mnvec`/`mrnxvec`, `mirq_entry`/
  `mintsel_jal`/`pushm*`. Deferred to the trap-bearing / S-U-envelope ROI work.
- `mppib`/`mfiob` (PPI/FIO base): platform-static; consistency check, not transport.

skills.name: simplify
skills.content:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

content.text:
Now let me compile my comprehensive findings report.

## SUMMARY

I've thoroughly explored the CSR round-trip test pattern in andesim. Here are your findings:

---

## 1. Full Source of `rt_csr_survival.S` Fixture

**File**: `/home/nick/work/andesim/tests/fixtures/rt_csr_survival.S` (79 lines)

The fixture demonstrates TWO assertion mechanisms:

**Phase 1 (QEMU1, lines 37-54)**: 
- Writes sentinel values to writable M-mode CSRs BEFORE the ROI entry marker
- `mscratch = 0xCAFEBABEDEADBEEF` (stored in callee-stable `a1` for in-ROI comparison)
- `mepc = 0x0000000080002340` (WARL, stored in `a4`)
- `mie = 0x0000000000000888` (MSIE|MTIE|MEIE bits, stored in `a5`)
- `mcause = 0x8000000000000007` (interrupt | code 7, for --verify only)
- `mtval = 0x0000000080001234` (for --verify only)
- Entry marker: `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (line 56)

**Phase 2 (vsim ROI, lines 58-69)**:
- **In-ROI self-check** (lines 59-64): Reads CSRs back and compares against saved values using `bne`. On mismatch, the fixture hangs (line 77-78), causing e2e timeout/failure.
- Overwrites `mscratch` with new sentinel `0xBADC0FFEE0DDF00D` (line 67) for StateDrain to capture
- Exit marker: `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (line 69)

**Verification coverage**:
- `mscratch`, `mepc`, `mie`: exact round-trip (in-ROI self-checked)
- `mcause` (WLRL), `mtval` (WARL): --verify only (oracle compares engine-vs-engine, not literal)
- NOT asserted: `mip` (hardware-driven bits) and S-mode CSRs (default engine M-only)

---

## 2. The Makefile Pattern: How Fixtures Are Built

**File**: `/home/nick/work/andesim/tests/fixtures/Makefile` (151 lines)

**Key sections**:

**Fixture families** (lines 28-50):
- `RT_FIXTURES` (asm): 10 fixtures including `rt_csr_survival`
- `RT_C_FIXTURES` (C-level): 5 fixtures linked through the vplat runtime
- `RT_C_V_FIXTURES` (V-extension C): 4 fixtures with `-march=rv64gcv`
- `RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES` (runtime smoke tests): 3 fixtures
- `BREAK_FIXTURES` (intentional bugs): 4 fixtures (not in default `all` target)

**Build pattern** (lines 98-100):
```makefile
$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
```
This is a **pattern rule**: a `.S` file automatically becomes a `.elf` without explicit per-fixture listing. All RT_FIXTURES are in the variables list (line 28-30); adding a new fixture means:
1. Create `new_fixture.S` in the same directory
2. Add it to the `RT_FIXTURES` variable line
3. `make` applies the pattern rule

**Compile flags**:
- `CFLAGS = -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall` (line 24)
- `LDSCRIPT = ../../runtime/andesim.ld` (load at 0x00100000)
- `LDFLAGS = -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static` (line 25)

**C-level fixtures** (lines 110-123):
- Linked with `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs` (user's exact command)
- Link against `libandesim_runtime.a` + `crt0.o` + `andesim.ld`
- Include path: `-I$(HELPERS_DIR)` for `rt_c_helpers.h`
- RVV fixtures use `-march=rv64gcv` separately (line 116)

---

## 3. ROI Marker Mechanics

**Header**: `/home/nick/work/andesim/runtime/ROI.h` (35 lines)

The markers are **RISC-V HINT instructions** (rd=x0 = architectural NOPs):
```c
static inline void andesim_ROI_begin(void)  // line 24
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}

static inline void andesim_ROI_end(void)    // line 29
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}
```

**Key contract**:
- `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` = ENTER ROI (QEMU1 drains + exits 200)
- `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` = EXIT ROI (vsim drains + exits 200)
- `"memory"` clobber prevents compiler from hoisting computation across markers
- Architecture-portable: same binary runs on fast, cycle, hybrid, AND silicon

**In assembly** (no macro needed): Direct `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` insns (e.g. rt_csr_survival.S lines 56, 69)

**In C**: `enter_vsim()` / `exit_vsim()` from `rt_c_helpers.h` (lines 55-62)

---

## 4. Verification (--verify) Mechanism

**Driver code**: `/home/nick/work/andesim/driver/state_diff.cpp` (128 lines)

**How it works**:

1. **Three-way run** (when `./andesim run --mode hybrid --verify`):
   - **Leg 1**: QEMU1 + plugin drain → `STATE_QEMU`
   - **Leg 2**: vsim resume+drain → `STATE_VSIM` (always runs)
   - **Leg 3**: Pure QEMU oracle run (marker or exit_pc trigger) → `STATE_ORACLE`

2. **Comparison** (in `diff_states()`, line 20):
   - Compares `STATE_ORACLE` (ref) vs `STATE_VSIM` (got)
   - Reports: `[state-diff] FIELD: ref=0xRRR got=0xGGG` for each mismatch (line 114)
   - Prints: `[state-diff] PASS: N fields match` on success (line 119)

3. **CSR coverage** (lines 30-44):
   - **Always compared**: `mepc`, `mcause`, `mscratch`, `mtval`, `mie`
   - **Excluded from verification**: `mip` (hardware-driven bits diverge)
   - **GPRs**: all 32 compared
   - **FPRs/fcsr**: compared if `HYBRID_FLAG_FP` set
   - **V regs/CSRs**: compared if `HYBRID_FLAG_V` set

4. **Andes V5 CSR block** (lines 96-107, F0):
   - **13 scalar CSRs** (via X-macro iteration, line 99): iterate `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)` from state_abi.h
   - **PMA arrays** (lines 101-106): `pmacfg[0..1]` + `pmaaddr[0..15]`
   - **Excluded from verify**: `msp_bound`, `msp_base` (HW stack protection diverges between engines; tolerant no-op on cores lacking it)
   - **Automatic comparison**: Writing an Andes CSR PRE-ROI → plugin drains → set `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES` → state_diff compares it

**No special fixture code needed**: If you write a CSR before the ROI, it round-trips automatically and --verify compares it.

---

## 5. ALL Existing Fixtures (31 total)

| **Family** | **Count** | **Fixtures** |
|-----------|---------|------------|
| **Asm (RT)** | 10 | `rt_all_gprs`, `rt_abi_aliases`, `rt_sign_bits`, `rt_pc_jump`, `rt_long_roi`, `rt_mem_loadstore`, `rt_unaligned_lh`, `rt_shared_mem`, `rt_csr_survival`, `rt_priv_smode`, `rt_priv_umode` |
| **C-level (rt_c_*)** | 5 | `rt_c_hello`, `rt_c_printf`, `rt_c_matmul`, `rt_c_static_buf`, `rt_c_fcsr` |
| **V-extension (rt_c_v_*)** | 4 | `rt_c_v_regs`, `rt_c_v_csrs`, `rt_c_v_matmul`, `rt_c_v_fill` |
| **Vplat smoke tests** | 3 | `vplat_hello`, `vplat_exit41`, `vplat_file` |
| **Other asm** | 3 | `spin`, `handoff`, `handoff_roundtrip` |
| **Break fixtures** (intentional bugs) | 4 | `break_vscratch`, `break_vscratch_top`, `break_mcycle_write`, `break_verify_diverge` |

---

## 6. Existing Fixtures Touching Andes CSRs

**Grep result**: NONE. 

No fixtures currently touch any Andes-specific CSRs. The only Andes CSR reference found was line 55 in `rt_c_printf.c` — a hexadecimal constant `0x80000000UL` in a format string, not an actual CSR write.

**List of Andes CSRs NOT yet tested**:
- mxstatus (0x7C4)
- mpft_ctl (0x7C5)
- mclk_ctl (0x7DF)
- milmb (0x7C0)
- mdlmb (0x7C1)
- mecc_code (0x7C2)
- mhsp_ctl (0x7C6)
- msp_bound (0x7C7)
- msp_base (0x7C8)
- mcountermask_m (0x7D1)
- uitb (0x800)
- jvt (0x017)
- ucode (0x801)
- PMA: pmacfg[0..1] (0xBC0, 0xBC2), pmaaddr[0..15] (0xBD0..0xBDF)

---

## Key Patterns to Copy for New Andes CSR Fixtures

### **Asm Pattern** (like rt_csr_survival.S):
```asm
// Phase 1: write before ROI
li      a1, <sentinel_value>
csrw    csr_name, a1            // write

slti    x0, x0, 0x5A0           // ENTER ROI

// Phase 2: read inside ROI (optional self-check)
csrr    a0, csr_name
bne     a0, a1, regress

// Phase 2: overwrite for drain (optional)
li      a2, <new_sentinel>
csrw    csr_name, a2

slti    x0, x0, 0x5A1           // EXIT ROI
```

### **C-level Pattern** (like rt_c_fcsr.c):
```c
#include "runtime/rt_c_helpers.h"

int main(void) {
  // Phase 1: write before ROI
  unsigned long set = 0x...;
  asm volatile("csrw csr_name, %0" ::"r"(set));
  
  enter_vsim();  // slti x0, x0, 0x5A0 with "memory" clobber
  
  // Phase 2: read inside ROI
  unsigned long got;
  asm volatile("csrr %0, csr_name" : "=r"(got));
  if (got != set) exit(1);
  
  // Phase 2: overwrite for drain
  asm volatile("csrw csr_name, %0" ::"r"(new_sentinel));
  
  exit_vsim();  // slti x0, x0, 0x5A1 with "memory" clobber
  
  return 0;
}
```

### **Build Integration**:
1. Create `tests/fixtures/rt_c_mxstatus.c` (or `.S` for asm)
2. Add to `RT_C_FIXTURES` (or `RT_FIXTURES`) variable in Makefile
3. Run `make -C tests/fixtures` → pattern rule builds `.elf` automatically

### **Verification**:
Run: `./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --verify tests/fixtures/rt_c_mxstatus.elf`

- `mtval = 0x0000000080001234` (for --verify only)

```c
{

}

static inline void andesim_ROI_end(void)    // line 29

```

- `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` = EXIT ROI (vsim drains + exits 200)

content.text:
Andes toolchain confirmed (`riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc 14.3.0`, V5): `rv64gcv_xandes` works, `exec.it` assembles. Tier-2 (DSP `add64`, `cm.jalt`) needs extra march extensions (`xandesdsp`/`zcmt`).

Decisive point: the **established "DONE" bar from F1** was a sentinel round-trip (`rt_csr_survival`, 144 fields) + unit tests — NOT the behavioral `exec.it` test (ROADMAP explicitly calls that a "remaining deeper check"). So "continue all features" = bring F2-F8 to that same bar. The transport code is already wired via the X-macro; what's missing is a fixture that writes a **non-reset** value (rt_csr_survival only round-trips reset defaults, so 0==0 proves nothing).

The crux is empirical: which Andes CSRs does `ax45mpv_premium` actually implement? An **empty-ROI probe fixture** that writes distinct sentinels to every candidate CSR and runs `--verify` maps it in one run (empty ROI = all writes side-effect-free). Let me read the exact fixture boilerplate first.

content.content:
1	// rt_csr_survival.S
2	//
3	// 2-phase guard (L23 + L24): the writable M-mode CSRs round-trip across the
4	// QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. A value stashed before the ROI is readable inside it
5	// (ResumeDriver restores the CSR) and a value written inside the ROI is
6	// captured at drain (StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough re-reads it).
7	//
8	// Covered CSRs:
9	//   L23  mscratch                 -- M-mode software scratch (pure read/write)
10	//   L24  mepc, mcause, mtval, mie -- writable trap/interrupt CSRs
11	//
12	// History: this fixture predates the 2-phase redesign. It used to read the CSRs
13	// back in a `phase_c` AFTER the exit marker and exit with the index of the
14	// first mismatch -- but once the QEMU2 handback leg was removed, vsim drains and
15	// exits AT the exit marker, so phase_c never ran and the guard was silently
16	// dead. The check now lives INSIDE the ROI, where the vsim leg actually runs.
17	//
18	// Two assertion mechanisms:
19	//   1. In-ROI self-check (works in the plain e2e harness, no --verify): read
20	//      the CSR back inside the ROI and `bne` against the stashed sentinel,
21	//      held in a callee-stable GPR which the GPR restore round-trips. On a
22	//      regressed restore the values differ, so the fixture spins -- vsim never
23	//      reaches the exit marker, times out, and the harness reports a failure.
24	//      Used only for mscratch/mepc/mie, whose values round-trip exactly.
25	//   2. --verify (VERIFY=1): the differential oracle compares the drained CSRs
26	//      against a pure-QEMU run. Used for mcause (WLRL) and mtval (WARL), whose
27	//      cross-engine legalisation could differ from a chosen sentinel; the
28	//      oracle path compares engine-against-engine instead of against a literal.
29	//
30	// Not asserted: mip (its pending bits are hardware-driven, not writable via
31	// csrw on an M-only core) and the S-mode CSRs medeleg/mideleg/satp (the default
32	// engine does not implement them). See docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb.
33	
34	.section .text
35	.globl _start
36	_start:
37	    // Stash sentinels into the writable M-mode CSRs BEFORE the ROI (QEMU leg).
38	    // a1/a4/a5 are callee-stable GPRs the restore round-trips, so the in-ROI
39	    // reads below can compare against them.
40	    li      a1, 0xCAFEBABEDEADBEEF
41	    csrw    mscratch, a1            // L23 software scratch CSR
42	
43	    li      a4, 0x0000000080002340  // aligned (bit0=0): mepc is WARL
44	    csrw    mepc, a4                // L24
45	    li      a5, 0x0000000000000888  // MSIE|MTIE|MEIE: standard M-mode mie bits
46	    csrw    mie, a5                 // L24 (mstatus.MIE stays 0: no trap is taken)
47	
48	    // mcause (WLRL, a legal cause) + mtval (WARL): set for --verify coverage,
49	    // not in-ROI self-checked (cross-engine legalisation may differ from the
50	    // literal; the oracle compares engine-vs-engine instead).
51	    li      t1, 0x8000000000000007  // interrupt | code 7 (M timer): legal cause
52	    csrw    mcause, t1
53	    li      t1, 0x0000000080001234
54	    csrw    mtval, t1
55	
56	    slti    x0, x0, 0x5A0           // ENTER ROI -> hand off to vsim
57	
58	    // Read the round-trip CSRs back INSIDE the ROI: each must be restored.
59	    csrr    a0, mscratch
60	    bne     a0, a1, regress         // restore lost? spin -> timeout -> test FAIL
61	    csrr    a3, mepc
62	    bne     a3, a4, regress
63	    csrr    a6, mie
64	    bne     a6, a5, regress
65	
66	    li      a2, 0xBADC0FFEE0DDF00D
67	    csrw    mscratch, a2            // overwrite; drain must re-read this value
68	
69	    slti    x0, x0, 0x5A1           // EXIT ROI -> vsim drains the CSRs, exits 200
70	
71	    // Unreached on hybrid (vsim stops at the exit marker). Engine-portable
72	    // SimControl exit so the same ELF still runs to completion standalone.
73	    li      t0, 0xe0080000
74	    sw      x0, 0(t0)
75	1:  j       1b
76	
77	regress:
78	    j       regress                 // a restored CSR is wrong: hang -> harness FAIL
79

1	// Shared exit-via-semihosting macro for hybrid round-trip fixtures.
2	//
3	// SEMIHOST_EXIT exit_reg
4	//   Builds the {reason=ADP_Stopped_ApplicationExit, exit_code=<exit_reg>}
5	//   16-byte block at 0x00001000, sets a0=SYS_EXIT_EXTENDED (0x20), a1=block,
6	//   then issues the RISC-V semihosting `slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`
7	//   triple. exit_reg may be any GPR holding the desired host exit code; this
8	//   macro clobbers t0, t1, a0, a1.
9	//
10	// QEMU's host-exit returns the low 8 bits of <exit_reg> as the process status.
11	
12	.macro SEMIHOST_EXIT exit_reg
13	    li      t0, 0x00001000
14	    li      t1, 0x20026                     // ADP_Stopped_ApplicationExit
15	    sd      t1, 0(t0)
16	    sd      \exit_reg, 8(t0)
17	    li      a0, 0x20                        // SYS_EXIT_EXTENDED
18	    mv      a1, t0
19	    .option push
20	    .option norvc
21	    slli    x0, x0, 0x1f
22	    ebreak
23	    srai    x0, x0, 0x7
24	    .option pop
25	99: j       99b
26	.endm

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).

BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

.PHONY: all clean dump

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (andesim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

content.text:
QEMU uses symbolic names (`CSR_MXSTATUS`, `CSR_UCODE`, ...) — my hex grep missed them, but the symbolic grep confirms QEMU's `andes-ax45mpv` cpu **implements every candidate CSR** (mxstatus, ucode, uitb, mpft_ctl, mhsp_ctl, mcountermask_m, milmb, mdlmb, msp_bound/base, PMA), each with a `WRITE_MASK_CSR_*` (WARL legalization). So `csrw` won't trap in the QEMU1 leg — a combined empty-ROI probe is safe.

Let me build a throwaway probe that writes a distinct sentinel to every feature's CSR and run `--verify`. The per-field diff maps, in one run, which CSRs the premium **vsim RTL** implements (got=sentinel) vs doesn't (got=0) vs WARL-masks.

// rt_andes_probe.S  (THROWAWAY)
// Empty-ROI transport probe: write a distinct sentinel to every candidate
// Andes V5 CSR in the QEMU1 leg, hand off, drain in vsim. `--verify` then
// reports, per field, whether the premium RTL round-trips the written value
// (got=sentinel), drops it (got=0 -> CSR not implemented in the engine), or
// WARL-masks it (got=partial). All writes are side-effect-free because the
// ROI between the markers is empty.

.section .text
.globl _start
_start:
    // --- F2 mxstatus 0x7C4 ---
    li      t0, 0x0000000000000040
    csrw    0x7c4, t0
    // --- F6 mpft_ctl 0x7C5 / mclk_ctl 0x7DF ---
    li      t0, 0x0000000000000100
    csrw    0x7c5, t0
    li      t0, 0x0000000000000003
    csrw    0x7df, t0
    // --- F5 milmb 0x7C0 / mdlmb 0x7C1 / mecc_code 0x7C2 (enable bit0=0) ---
    li      t0, 0x0000000000200000
    csrw    0x7c0, t0
    li      t0, 0x0000000000400000
    csrw    0x7c1, t0
    li      t0, 0x0000000000000007
    csrw    0x7c2, t0
    // --- F7 mhsp_ctl 0x7C6 / msp_bound 0x7C7 / msp_base 0x7C8 ---
    li      t0, 0x0000000000000010
    csrw    0x7c6, t0
    li      t0, 0x00000000DEAD0000
    csrw    0x7c7, t0
    li      t0, 0x00000000BA5E0000
    csrw    0x7c8, t0
    // --- F8 mcountermask_m 0x7D1 ---
    li      t0, 0x0000000000000004
    csrw    0x7d1, t0
    // --- F1 controls: uitb 0x800 / jvt 0x017 (already DONE) ---
    li      t0, 0x0000000000001000
    csrw    0x800, t0
    li      t0, 0x0000000000002040
    csrw    0x017, t0
    // --- F4 ucode 0x801 (P-ext gated) ---
    li      t0, 0x0000000000000001
    csrw    0x801, t0
    // --- F3 PMA pmacfg0/2 0xBC0/0xBC2, pmaaddr0/1 0xBD0/0xBD1 ---
    li      t0, 0x0000000000000018
    csrw    0xbc0, t0
    li      t0, 0x0000000000000024
    csrw    0xbc2, t0
    li      t0, 0x00000000000ABCDE
    csrw    0xbd0, t0
    li      t0, 0x00000000000ABCD1
    csrw    0xbd1, t0

    slti    x0, x0, 0x5A0           // ENTER ROI (empty)
    slti    x0, x0, 0x5A1           // EXIT ROI -> vsim drains, exits

    // Portable standalone exit (unreached on hybrid).
    li      t0, 0xe0080000
    sw      x0, 0(t0)
1:  j       1b

content.text:
The empty-ROI run **timed out in the vsim leg** (90s). Key insight: vsim is cycle-accurate, so it *honors* control CSRs the moment they're restored — even with an empty ROI, the hart runs between resume and the exit marker. Writing `mclk_ctl` (clock control), `mpft_ctl` (throttle), or `mhsp_ctl` (stack-protection trap) likely stalls or faults the hart. The QEMU1 leg (functional) ignored them, so the writes themselves succeeded.

I need to distinguish a **transport bug** (DMI restore of an unimplemented CSR hangs — would affect everything, must fix in `resume_driver`) from an **expected execution effect** (test wrote a clock-gating value). Bisect: data-only probe (drop the 6 control CSRs).

content.text:
Still hangs with **data-only** CSRs — so it's not a control-CSR execution effect. The hang is triggered by restoring some **non-zero** Andes CSR via DMI into premium. Critical realization: F1's "validation" (rt_csr_survival, 144 fields) round-tripped uitb/jvt at value **0** (the fixture never writes them) — so *no Andes CSR has ever been round-tripped at a non-zero value before this probe*. This is the first, and it hangs.

A correct `write_csr_tolerant` should no-op a write to an absent CSR (clean `got=0` diff, no hang). A hang suggests it polls a DMI abstract-command error forever — a **transport bug** (root cause to fix, not avoid). Let me isolate the culprit CSR with parallel single-CSR probes (independent vsim processes, parallel 90s waits).

Now I have real data. The map:

| Probe | Result | Meaning |
|-------|--------|---------|
| **uitb** | PASS | non-zero round-trips cleanly (F1 now truly validated at non-zero) |
| **ucode** | **HANG** | restoring an absent CSR hangs vsim |
| **mecccode** | **HANG** | same hang |
| **mcntmask** | FAIL `got=0x0` | engine lacks it but **cleanly no-ops** (no hang) |
| **pmaaddr0** | FAIL `ref=0xabcde got=0xabc00` | implemented, but QEMU/vsim **disagree on WARL** masking |
| **pmacfg0** | FAIL `ref=0x18 got=0xc` | implemented, WARL legalizes differently |

The headline bug: **restoring some absent CSRs (ucode, mecc_code) HANGS, while another absent CSR (mcountermask) cleanly no-ops to 0.** `write_csr_tolerant` is not uniformly tolerant. That's a root-cause transport bug — it must no-op cleanly for *any* absent CSR. Let me read how restore handles the failing write.
